issues.legal_issue: A partial payment or deposit toward a money decree stops further interest on the portion paid, and a shortfall is ordinarily appropriated first to interest, then costs, and then principal.
material_facts: The judgment considered payments and deposits made in execution of decrees for money that did not necessarily satisfy the full decretal amount.
The applicable procedural rules provide for notice to the decree-holder of a court deposit and cessation of interest on the amount deposited.
The Court distinguished the allocation of a shortfall from reopening amounts already satisfied by a payment or deposit.
issues.conclusion: For a money decree other than a mortgage decree, interest ceases on the portion deposited once the required notice is given, and the decree-holder cannot reopen satisfaction of that portion. If a deposit falls short and no contrary direction applies, the shortfall is appropriated first to interest, then costs, and then principal.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 1, particularly its provisions on notice and cessation of interest as amended in 1976, read in the context of Order XXIV Rules 1 to 4, governs post-decree payments. The amendment makes interest cease on the deposited portion after notice, rather than permitting reappropriation of prior deposits. Sections 59 to 61 of the Contract Act govern appropriation among multiple debts at the pre-decree stage, not a debt merged in a decree. The Court relied on Industrial Credit & Development Syndicate Ltd. v. Smithaben H. Patel, Meghraj v. Mst. Bayabai, and Mathunni Mathai v. Hindustan Organic Chemicals Ltd.; it explained that Mathunni Mathai concerned when interest ceases, not the allocation of payments under an award decree.

predicates.money_decree_execution: The proceeding is to enforce a decree requiring payment of money, rather than a mortgage decree.
predicates.partial_payment_or_deposit: The judgment-debtor paid or deposited an amount that did not necessarily satisfy the entire decree.
predicates.required_notice_given: The decree-holder received the notice of the payment or deposit required for interest to cease.

issues.definition: When a judgment-debtor partly pays or deposits money toward a money decree and the decree-holder receives the required notice, interest stops on the portion paid or deposited.

issues.legal_issue: Amounts satisfied at an earlier stage of a land-acquisition compensation award cannot be reopened and reappropriated merely because compensation is enhanced at a later stage.
material_facts: The statutory scheme determines compensation first through the Collector and may later result in enhancement by a reference court and appellate courts.
The Collector’s award and the later awards contain distinct components of compensation, interest, and costs.
The issue was whether amounts paid or deposited at an earlier stage could be reallocated after a later enhancement so that interest would be recalculated on the whole enhanced amount.
The Court held that the award and deposit structure provides for payment at successive stages and does not permit a general reopening of earlier satisfaction.
issues.conclusion: A claimant cannot reopen amounts paid or deposited and satisfied at an earlier stage to reappropriate them against compensation awarded at a later stage. Each later enhancement is dealt with at that stage, and interest is payable on the enhanced amount as provided by the governing scheme.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 23, 26, 28, 34, 53, and 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, read with Order XXI Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, provide for distinct components of compensation and successive stages of determination and payment. The Court approved the appropriation reasoning in Prem Nath Kapur v. National Fertilizers Corporation of India, while explaining that Sunder v. Union of India, which held that compensation includes the components specified in Section 23, did not displace that reasoning. It also held that the doctrine of merger does not override the statutory scheme. Mathunni Mathai did not decide the allocation issue.

rule.if: land_acquisition_award_execution and compensation_determined_at_multiple_stages and earlier_stage_amount_satisfied and later_stage_enhancement_awarded

predicates.land_acquisition_award_execution: The proceeding is to execute an award or decree determining compensation for an acquired land interest.
predicates.compensation_determined_at_multiple_stag: Compensation was determined at an initial stage and was capable of further determination on reference or appeal.
predicates.earlier_stage_amount_satisfied: The amount awarded at an earlier stage was paid or deposited and the decree-holder received it or had the required notice of deposit.
predicates.later_stage_enhancement_awarded: A later decision increased the compensation payable.

issues.definition: When compensation in a land-acquisition proceeding is determined and satisfied at one stage before a later enhancement, the earlier satisfaction cannot be reopened to recalculate the amount payable.

issues.legal_issue: A shortfall in a deposit toward an award decree may be appropriated first to interest, then costs, and then principal, unless the decree or the debtor’s communicated designation requires a different allocation.
material_facts: The Court considered the possibility that the amount deposited at a particular stage of a land-acquisition proceeding would fall short of the amount then payable.
It held that the ordinary appropriation rule applies to the shortfall, subject to a direction in the decree or an indication that the deposit is for specified heads of compensation.
The Court distinguished allocating a shortfall from reopening amounts already satisfied at an earlier stage.
issues.conclusion: For a shortfall at a particular stage, the decree-holder may appropriate the amount first toward interest, then costs, and then principal, unless the decree directs otherwise or the debtor has indicated that the deposit is for specified heads.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the general post-decree appropriation rule under Order XXI Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as explained in the judgment, alongside the staged scheme of Sections 23, 26, 28, and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. Prem Nath Kapur v. National Fertilizers Corporation of India was approved as to staged appropriation, with the qualification that a shortfall at a particular stage may be allocated under the general rule unless a contrary direction or communicated designation applies.

rule.if: award_decree_execution and deposit_shortfall_at_current_stage and not contrary_allocation_direction and not communicated_specific_designation

predicates.award_decree_execution: The proceeding is to execute an award decree requiring payment of compensation and related amounts.
predicates.deposit_shortfall_at_current_stage: The amount deposited for the amounts payable at the current stage is insufficient to meet them in full.
predicates.contrary_allocation_direction: The decree directs an allocation different from the ordinary order of appropriation.
predicates.communicated_specific_designation: The debtor communicated that the deposit was intended for specified heads of the amount payable.

issues.definition: If a deposit toward an award decree falls short at the relevant stage and neither the decree nor the debtor specifies a different allocation, the shortfall is applied first to interest, then costs, and then principal.

issues.legal_issue: An amount withdrawn under an interim appellate order is appropriated according to any allocation directed by that order or, absent such a direction, first to interest, then costs, and then principal if the appeal is ultimately decided in the awardee’s favour.
material_facts: An awardee may receive part of an award amount under an interim order while an appeal or further appeal is pending.
The appropriation of such a withdrawal remains subject to the result of the appeal and any allocation stated in the interim order.

The Court held that, if the appeal is decided in the awardee’s favour and the interim order did not specify an allocation, the amount is applied first to interest, then costs, and then principal as of the date of withdrawal; interest ceases on the part applied to principal.
issues.conclusion: If the appeal is decided in the awardee’s favour, an interim withdrawal is appropriated first to interest, then costs, and then principal as of withdrawal, unless the interim order specifies another allocation. Interest ceases on the portion applied to principal from the date of receipt.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the general appropriation rule for a decree payment, subject to the terms of the interim order and the result of the appeal, in the context of the staged compensation scheme under Sections 28 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. The Court’s approval of the staged appropriation approach in Prem Nath Kapur v. National Fertilizers Corporation of India is consistent with this treatment of interim withdrawals.

predicates.awardee_withdrew_amount_under_interim_or: The awardee received an amount under an interim order while an appeal was pending.
predicates.appeal_decided_in_awardee_favour: The appeal was ultimately decided in a way that entitled the awardee to the amount awarded.
predicates.no_interim_allocation_direction: The interim order did not direct how the withdrawn amount was to be appropriated.

issues.definition: When an awardee receives money under an interim order and the appeal is decided in the awardee’s favour, the amount is applied first to interest, then costs, and then principal if the interim order did not specify another allocation.

issues.legal_issue: An execution court may allow interest on solatium when the decree awards interest on compensation without expressly or implicitly rejecting interest on solatium, but it cannot grant that relief after the execution has closed.
material_facts: The Court considered whether an awardee could seek interest on solatium in execution when the decree did not specifically grant that interest.
It held that an execution court cannot go behind the decree and must reject the claim if the reference court or appellate court expressly or by necessary implication rejected it.
Where the decree does not address the issue, or the claim was not made and rejected, the execution court may apply Sunder and treat compensation as including solatium.
The Court limited this relief to pending executions and clarified that it did not permit reappropriation or fresh appropriation.
issues.conclusion: In a pending execution, the execution court may allow interest on solatium if the decree does not specifically address that interest or the claim was not made and rejected, expressly or by necessary implication. The claim must be rejected if the decree did reject it, and it is unavailable in a closed execution.
issues.legal_principle: Sunder v. Union of India held that compensation includes the components under Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and interest may therefore be payable on solatium when the decree does not foreclose that claim. The principle that an execution court cannot go behind the decree bars relief where interest on solatium was expressly or implicitly rejected. The Court stated this clarification in exercise of its powers under Articles 141 and 142 of the Constitution of India and limited it to pending executions, without authorizing reappropriation.

rule.if: land_acquisition_award_execution and execution_pending and decree_awards_interest_on_compensation and not interest_on_solatium_rejected

predicates.land_acquisition_award_execution: The proceeding is to execute an award or decree determining compensation for an acquired land interest.
predicates.execution_pending: The execution proceeding remains open and has not been closed.
predicates.decree_awards_interest_on_compensation: The decree awards interest on compensation without specifically resolving the treatment of solatium.
predicates.interest_on_solatium_rejected: The reference court or appellate court expressly or by necessary implication rejected a claim for interest on solatium.

issues.definition: In a pending execution of an award decree that grants interest on compensation, interest on solatium may be allowed if the decree has not rejected that claim.
